item.title: Dry Danube River threatens nuclear power in Romania, Hungary
item.description: Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant was operating at about 10% of capacity because of a lack of cooling riverwater. In Romania, the military blew up a rock outcrop in a bid to improve water flow to the Cernavoda plant.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Ceuta: EU calls borders a 'shared European responsibility'
item.description: The European Commission has offered Morocco more support at the border to Ceuta and Melilla, and called for "united action" from the bloc on border security. Its interior ministers will discuss the issue on Tuesday.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Can PM Modi reconnect with India's Gen Z?
item.description: Student protests exposed a growing disconnect between PM Narendra Modi's BJP and young Indians. Experts say Instagram reels alone won't close it.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Russia: Bridge-building with North Korea
item.description: In the far east, well away from world events, Russia and North Korea are building their first road connection. The project has set alarm bells ringing in Ukraine.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Cuba suffers yet another nationwide blackout
item.description: Cuba's electricity grid has collapsed again after three nationwide blackouts in July. The power failure comes amid a US-imposed oil blockade on the communist island.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Man arrested over death of British woman found in suitcase in Athens
item.description: The body of Scottish national Elisabeth-Jane Ross was discovered last month in a suitcase in a derelict building in Athens.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Small insects, big damage: The global ant trade is booming
item.description: Legal or not, the trade in African ants bound for Europe is booming. What do hobbyists find appealing about these insects, and what risks does the trade pose to ecosystems, including power outages?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Moscow restaurant blast a 'brutal terror attack,' mayor says
item.description: The deadly explosion outside an upscale Moscow restaurant at Kudrinskaya Square was a "brutal terror attack," Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said, promising the perpetrators would be punished. But many questions remain.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Poland: Prime Minister Tusk defies anti-Ukrainian violence
item.description: Anti-Ukrainian sentiment in Poland is on the rise, with numerous attacks against refugees from the war in Ukraine. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has spoken out against the violence and warned of the danger from Russia.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: On the front line of Europe's battle against wildfires
item.description: French firefighters have won out over a massive blaze, with almost 200,000 evacuees returning home. But Europe's climate-fueled wildfire season is far from over.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Hungary to shut sole nuclear plant for first time on Sunday
item.description: Record-low water levels on the Danube forced the Paks plant offline, leaving Hungary facing a potential power crunch. In neighboring Serbia, energy production at two hydroelectric plants has also been reduced.

item.title: How does eastern Europe commemorate the Roma Holocaust?
item.description: In 2015, the EU designated August 2 as the European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day. In Germany, the day is marked with memorial services, educational activites and public addresses. And in eastern Europe?
